name: AI Model Release Timeline
title: AI Model Release Timeline: 159 LLMs, 2018 to 2026
h1: AI Model Release Timeline: Every Major LLM From GPT-1 to GPT-6 (2018-2026)
description: AI model release timeline of 159 LLMs from GPT-1 to GPT-6: release dates, open weights, context windows and launch API prices, each linked to the lab's source.
summary: Release dates, open-weight status, context windows, input types and launch API prices for 159 notable LLMs from 2018 to October 2026, each sourced to the lab.
intro: ChatGPT was released on November 30, 2022, as a free research preview built on a GPT-3.5 model, according to [OpenAI's announcement](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt/); developers got the same model through the API on March 1, 2023, at $2 per million tokens. This AI model release timeline covers 159 notable large language models, from OpenAI's GPT-1 (June 11, 2018) to GPT-6.1 Terra (October 26, 2026), with release date, open-weight status, context window, input types and launch API price for each, every row linked to the lab's own announcement, model card or documentation.

The pace has changed most since 2023. The table holds 19 releases from 2023, 35 from 2024, 44 from 2025 and 51 from January through October 2026. Context windows grew from 512 tokens for GPT-1 to about 1 million tokens for 39 of the 51 models released in 2026, and the price of a top OpenAI model fell from $30 per million input tokens for GPT-4 in March 2023 to $2 for GPT-6.1 Sol in September 2026. Of the 159 rows, 82 are open-weight releases, led by Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen team and Moonshot AI.

The table is sortable and downloadable as CSV or JSON. Release date means the first day the model was publicly usable (in an app, through an API, or as downloadable weights), not the day a paper or teaser appeared. Prices are the lab's standard list price per million tokens on launch day; a dash means the lab did not sell API access or did not publish a price.

keyFindings.text: OpenAI released ChatGPT on November 30, 2022, as a free research preview based on a GPT-3.5 model fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from human feedback.
GPT-4 launched on March 14, 2023, with an 8,192-token context window at $0.03 per 1,000 prompt tokens and $0.06 per 1,000 completion tokens ($30 and $60 per million), according to OpenAI.
Google's Gemini 1.5 Pro became the first model offered through a public API with a 1-million-token context window when it entered public preview in the Gemini API on April 9, 2024.

source.title: Google Developers Blog: Gemini 1.5 Pro now available in 180+ countries

keyFindings.text: DeepSeek released the open-weight reasoning model DeepSeek-R1 under the MIT License on January 20, 2025, with API prices of $0.55 per million input tokens (cache miss) and $2.19 per million output tokens.

source.title: DeepSeek-R1 Release (DeepSeek API news, archived copy)

keyFindings.text: Meta released Llama 4 Scout on April 5, 2025, with a 10-million-token context window, the longest of any model in this dataset.
OpenAI's gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, released on August 5, 2025, under the Apache 2.0 license, were the company's first open-weight language models since GPT-2 in 2019.
Anthropic cut the price of its Opus tier from $15 and $75 per million input and output tokens to $5 and $25 with Claude Opus 4.5 on November 24, 2025.

OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026, and GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on September 22, 2026, with Luna priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, according to its API changelog.
Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026, with a 1-million-token context window at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20% below Claude Opus 5.

Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, released on July 16, 2026, is a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model whose weights Moonshot published under its own Kimi K3 License, with API prices of $3 and $15 per million input and output tokens.

source.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence (Moonshot AI)

sections.heading: AI model releases per year, by lab
sections.body:
The table below counts the rows in this dataset by lab and calendar year (2026 runs through October 29). It measures what this timeline includes, not every checkpoint a lab has shipped: minor dated snapshots, fine-tunes and most size variants are folded into one row.

| Lab | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 4 | 8 | 8 | 27 |
| Anthropic | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 6 | 12 | 24 |
| Google | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 15 |
| Meta | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 4 | 2 | 4 | 14 |
| xAI | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 7 |
| Mistral AI | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 13 |
| DeepSeek | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 8 |
| Alibaba Qwen | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 9 |
| Moonshot AI | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Microsoft | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| Amazon | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 4 |
| Other Chinese labs | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 6 | 5 | 13 |
| Other labs (Cohere, AI21, NVIDIA, others) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 5 | 1 | 4 | 15 |
| **All rows** | **2** | **2** | **1** | **1** | **4** | **19** | **35** | **44** | **51** | **159** |

Two patterns stand out. Release cadence at the largest labs roughly doubled between 2024 and 2026: Anthropic has 12 rows in 2026 against 3 in 2024, and OpenAI moved to new model families every few months (GPT-5.4 in March, GPT-5.5 in April, GPT-5.6 in July and GPT-6 in September 2026). And Chinese labs outside DeepSeek, Qwen and Moonshot (Z.ai, MiniMax, Xiaomi, Baidu, Tencent, ByteDance) went from one row in 2024 to six in 2025, almost all of them open-weight.

sections.heading: How context windows and API prices have changed
sections.body:
**Context windows grew about 2,000-fold in eight years.** Documented launch figures in the table:

| Date | Model | Context window (tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| 2018-06 | [GPT-1](https://openai.com/index/language-unsupervised/) | 512 |
| 2020-06 | [GPT-3](https://openai.com/index/openai-api/) | 2,048 |
| 2023-03 | [GPT-4](https://openai.com/index/gpt-4-research/) | 8,192 (32,768 for gpt-4-32k) |
| 2023-07 | [Claude 2](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-2) | 100,000 |
| 2023-11 | [GPT-4 Turbo](https://openai.com/index/new-models-and-developer-products-announced-at-devday/) | 128,000 |
| 2023-11 | [Claude 2.1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-2-1) | 200,000 |
| 2024-04 | [Gemini 1.5 Pro](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/gemini-15-pro-now-available-in-180-countries-with-native-audio-understanding-system-instructions-json-mode-and-more/) | 1,000,000 |
| 2025-04 | [Llama 4 Scout](https://ai.meta.com/blog/llama-4-multimodal-intelligence/) | 10,000,000 |
| 2026-03 | [GPT-5.4](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog) | 1,050,000 |

One million tokens has become the default rather than the exception. No 2023 row reaches 1 million tokens; 2 of 35 rows in 2024 do, 10 of 44 in 2025, and 39 of 51 in 2026. Opus-class Claude models reached 1 million tokens with [Claude Opus 4.6](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-6) in February 2026, in beta at launch.

**Prices for a given capability tier fell sharply, while the top tier did not get cheaper.** OpenAI's flagship input price dropped from $30 per million tokens for GPT-4 (March 2023) to $10 for GPT-4 Turbo (November 2023), $5 for GPT-4o (May 2024) and $2 for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6.1 Sol (September 2026). Small models fell further: GPT-4o mini launched at $0.15 input and $0.60 output in July 2024, and GPT-6 Luna at $0.10 and $0.50 in September 2026. Anthropic's Opus tier went from $15 and $75 ([Claude 3 Opus](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family), March 2024) to $5 and $25 ([Claude Opus 4.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-5), November 2025) and $4 and $20 ([Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5), September 2026). OpenAI cut o3's price by 80% on June 10, 2025, less than two months after launch.

At the same time, labs added more expensive tiers above their previous flagships. GPT-4.5 launched at $75 and $150 per million tokens in February 2025, the highest list price in the table. In 2026, GPT-6 Astra ($10 and $50), Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 ($10 and $50) and the restricted Claude Mythos Preview ($25 and $125 for partners) sit above the mainstream price points. Chinese open-weight models are priced lower: DeepSeek-V4-Flash listed at $0.14 and $0.28 per million tokens in April 2026.

Launch list prices are only a partial guide to cost. Reasoning models bill their thinking tokens as output, so the cost of a task depends on how many tokens a model writes, and introductory prices (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash) rise after a set date.

sections.heading: Open weights versus open source
sections.body:
"Open weights" in this table means the trained model parameters can be downloaded and run on your own hardware. It says nothing about the license, the training data or the training code, and those differ widely between models marked "Yes".

- **Permissive licenses.** Apache 2.0 (Mistral 7B, Mixtral, gpt-oss, Qwen3, Gemma 4) and MIT (DeepSeek-R1 and V4, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, GLM-4.5) allow commercial use and modification with few conditions.
- **Custom community licenses.** Meta's Llama licenses allow commercial use but require companies whose products had more than 700 million monthly active users to request a separate license from Meta ([Llama 3 license](https://dev.meta.ai/llama/llama3/license/)). Kimi K3, Qwen3.8-Max, GLM-5.3 and Muse Spark Open also ship under lab-specific licenses with their own conditions.
- **Non-commercial or research licenses.** OPT-175B, the first LLaMA, Command R, Command R+, Command A, Codestral and Mistral Large 2 published weights for research or non-commercial use only.

Open source is a stricter standard. The [Open Source Initiative's Open Source AI Definition 1.0](https://opensource.org/ai/open-source-ai-definition), released in October 2024, requires the model parameters, the complete code used to train and run the system, and enough detail about the training data for a skilled person to build a substantially equivalent system, all under OSI-approved terms. Most open-weight models publish the weights and inference code but not the training data or full training pipeline, so they meet the first condition and not the others. Ai2's [OLMo](https://allenai.org/blog/olmo-open-language-model-87ccfc95f580), which released its training data, code, logs and checkpoints alongside the weights, is an example of a fuller release.

For anyone choosing among the best open-weight models, the license column matters as much as benchmark scores: check whether commercial use, fine-tuning, hosting for third parties and use of outputs to train other models are allowed before deploying.

methodology: Scope: notable large language model releases from 2018 to October 29, 2026, chosen to cover each major lab's main generations (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI, Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen team, Moonshot AI, Microsoft, Amazon, Cohere, AI21 Labs and leading Chinese labs) plus influential open-weight releases from EleutherAI, BigScience, TII, Ai2, NVIDIA and Thinking Machines Lab. Image, video and speech-only models are excluded. Minor dated snapshots and most size variants are merged into one row, so per-lab counts measure this dataset, not total output.

Sources: each row cites the lab's own announcement, model card, Hugging Face card, documentation or API changelog, read during compilation on October 29, 2026. Where one field came from a second official page from the same lab (for example a pricing page or model docs page for the context window), that page was also checked. Three rows (Qwen3-Max-Preview, Qwen3.5 and ERNIE 4.5) cite reputable technology press because no dated official English announcement was found. DeepSeek-R1 cites an archived copy of DeepSeek's own news page, because the live URL now redirects. Wikipedia and third-party trackers were not used as sources.

Release date is the first day the model was publicly usable: in a consumer app, through an API (including public previews), or as downloadable weights. Where a model was announced earlier for limited testing, the note says so (for example, Gemini 1.5 Pro was announced February 15, 2024, and Gemini 4 Argon on September 30, 2026, to a restricted program). Dates shown as YYYY-MM have a documented month but no single documented day.

Prices are the standard list price per million tokens on the lab's own API at launch, before caching, batch or off-peak discounts. Prices quoted per 1,000 tokens in older announcements were multiplied by 1,000. Where a lab launched with an introductory price (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5), the introductory price is shown and the note says so. Tiered prices show the lowest tier (for example, Claude Haiku 5.5 for prompts up to 100,000 tokens and Gemini 3 Pro up to 200,000). For a few recent OpenAI and Google models, the price comes from the current pricing page and the changelog records no change since launch. DeepSeek-V3 launched at promotional V2 rates; the row shows its standard price, which took effect February 8, 2025. Prices in Chinese yuan only were left blank rather than converted.

Values not stated by an official source are left blank, never estimated: this includes several Anthropic context windows from 2023 to 2025, most Amazon Nova prices and many open-weight models' prices because their labs offered no API at launch. Context windows are the documented launch maximum, so later extensions are not shown. Counts in the text are computed from the rows in this table. xAI's 2026 announcements appear under the SpaceXSI brand on x.ai; the rows keep the label xAI for continuity.

faq.a: ChatGPT was released on November 30, 2022, as a free research preview, according to OpenAI. It ran on a model from the GPT-3.5 series fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from human feedback. Developers got API access to the same model, gpt-3.5-turbo, on March 1, 2023, at $0.002 per 1,000 tokens. GPT-4 followed on March 14, 2023, and GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026.

faq.q: What is the latest AI model released?
faq.a: As of October 29, 2026, the most recent releases in this timeline are OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra (October 26, 2026), Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro (October 24), Meta's Muse Spark Open (October 15), Google's Gemini 4 Argon (generally available October 13) and Meta's Muse Wonder (October 12). New frontier models now arrive every few weeks, so check the release date column for the current order.

faq.q: What are the best open-weight models?
faq.a: Among 2026 releases, the largest open-weight models in this table include Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 (2.8 trillion parameters), Alibaba's Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6 trillion), Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro, Thinking Machines' Inkling and Meta's Muse Spark Open. Which is best depends on the task, hardware and license; MiMo-V2.6-Pro and DeepSeek V4 use the permissive MIT license, while Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 use custom licenses.

faq.q: What is the difference between open weights and open source AI?
faq.a: Open-weight models let anyone download the trained parameters, often under licenses that restrict some uses. Open source AI, as defined by the Open Source Initiative in October 2024, also requires the full training and inference code and enough information about the training data to rebuild a substantially equivalent model, all under OSI-approved terms. Most open-weight LLMs, including Llama and many Chinese models, do not meet that full definition.

faq.q: Which AI model has the largest context window?
faq.a: In this dataset, Meta's Llama 4 Scout, released April 5, 2025, has the largest documented context window at 10 million tokens. Most 2026 frontier models, including Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon and DeepSeek V4, offer about 1 million tokens. For comparison, GPT-4 launched in March 2023 with 8,192 tokens, and GPT-1 handled 512.

There is no fixed count, because labs release new checkpoints, sizes and fine-tunes constantly, and anyone can publish fine-tuned versions of open-weight models. This list of LLMs tracks 159 notable releases from 26 organizations between June 2018 and October 2026, merging minor variants into one row. Of those, 82 shipped with downloadable weights and 77 were available only through apps or APIs.

faq.q: How have AI model prices changed over time?
faq.a: Prices for a given tier have fallen steeply. GPT-4 cost $30 per million input tokens in March 2023; GPT-6 Sol cost $2 in September 2026, and GPT-6 Luna $0.10. Anthropic's Opus tier fell from $15 and $75 per million input and output tokens in 2024 to $4 and $20 with Claude Opus 5.5. Labs have also added premium tiers, such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 at $10 and $50.
